items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear (updateAfterSalePreview, executeDangerAction, findProductAndVariant) and sections have banner comments. But template strings carry long inline style attributes, and the refund-allocation preview has almost no comments.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: index.html is one 3176-line file (cap applies). updateAfterSalePreview re-implements the refund-allocation and 'all items refunded' logic instead of calling the shared requestAfterSale path. The already-refunded reduce is copy-pasted between the modal and the preview.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Inputs are checked (parseInt with isNaN, empty import text, API returns ok:false with an error). The clipboard catch shows a toast. Some magic values remain (10% member rate inline, min=0 inputs), and preview clamping with Math.min hides edge cases instead of validating them.

items.name: Clerk workbench usability: amount breakdown, status hints, dangerous-action confirmation
items.name_zh: 店员工作台可用性：金额明细、状态提示与危险操作确认
items.evidence: Has a danger modal for restock and reset, plus status-specific actions and a refund preview showing the formula. But submitAfterSale submits refunds with no confirmation step, and doImportData overwrites data directly without a confirm.

items.name: Business logic lives in one place (UI and test API share it; integer-cent money)
items.name_zh: 业务逻辑集中且被界面与测试接口共用（金额按分计算）
items.evidence: The UI calls shopAPI.* for actions, so the API is the real logic. Money is float math with round2 ('(sumOriginal * order.payable) / order.subtotal', 'round2(order.payable - order.refundedAmount)'), not integer cents. The UI preview duplicates the refund calculation.
